title: Release engineering meeting notes 2026-08-18
content:
Date: 2026-08-18
Time: 10:00-11:00 PT
Location: Zoom / #release-engineering
Attendees: Jordan Kim (owner), Priya Desai, Marcus Liu, Elena García, Samir Patel, + guests from SRE (K. Novak)
Absentees: None noted

Agenda:
- Weekly sync: release trains and scheduling
- Hotfix status and rollback/mitigation updates
- Change log updates and release notes owner assignment
- Canary plan for v2026.08.1
- Action items and next steps

Notes:
1) Release trains
- Target train: v2026.08.1 (features + infra tweaks) scheduled for 2026-08-25, 1400 PT deploy window. Standby date 2026-08-26 if any last-minute blockers.
- Primary contents: batching kernel improvements (PR #578), improved KV cache eviction tuning, and observability tag changes for per-model metrics.
- Risk assessment: batching kernel change has moderate risk (regression surface in latency under mixed short/long sequence traffic). We discussed gating with an extended canary (see canary plan below).
- Rollout plan: 10% canary for first 2 hours -> 30% next 4 hours if no regressions -> 100% after 24h of stable metrics. Automatic rollback on latency SLA breach (>20% P95 over baseline for 30m) or error rate spike (>2x baseline).

2) Hotfixes
- Hotfix for v2026.07.9: a customer-reported tokenizer edge-case (JIRA RLS-1245) was fixed and hotfixed on 2026-08-16. Deployed to prod region us-west1.
  - Post-deploy: minimal customer impact; monitor the error bucket for tokenizer failures. SRE will keep watch until 2026-08-20.
- New hotfix candidate: RLS-1250 - observed KV-cache eviction thrash under heavy prefix-cache workloads causing elevated CPU on certain Dedicated nodes. Marcus to own triage and create a minimal hotfix branch if needed.

3) Change log / release notes
- Priya to own the release notes for v2026.08.1. Draft due by 2026-08-22 EOD. Include sections: notable fixes, breaking changes (none expected), performance notes (quantified token/sec change from batching kernel), and customer impact table.
- Add hotfix entries for v2026.07.9 (RLS-1245) and any follow-ups from RLS-1250. Maintain short customer-facing summary + internal detailed notes.

4) Canary and rollout specifics (detailed)
- Canary cohort selection: include a mix of hosted API traffic (small/medium requests) and dedicated customers with low-trafficking workloads. Avoid highest-SLA enterprise customers for initial canary.
- Metrics to monitor during canary: P95 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, model token/sec, and per-model request timeout counts. Grafana dashboard: release/canary/v2026.08.1 (Elena to create if missing).
- Alerting thresholds: P95 +20% -> immediate pause and investigation; error rate >2x -> immediate rollback; GPU utilization >85% sustained for 15m -> investigate batching behavior.

5) Outstanding blockers
- Load test gap: we still need a verification run for mixed-sequence workloads (short+long). Elena will run a 3-hour synthetic test using the bench harness by 2026-08-20 and post results in the ticket.
- Infra config: infra PR #612 modifies autoscaler thresholds. Infra owner (Samir) will ensure rollback hooks are in place and autoscaler tests pass in staging by 2026-08-21.
- Cherrypick risk: batching kernel PR touches low-level runtime; Marcus to identify minimal cherrypick for hotfix vs full kernel update.

6) Post-release and cleanup
- After 100% rollout, run a focused 48h monitoring window (team on-call rotation). Jordan to coordinate on-call schedule and handoff.
- Documentation: Update the runbook for rolling back v2026.08.X trains (Samir). Include steps for emergency rollback, partial model pinning, and quick hotfix creation flow.

Decisions made:
- Proceed with v2026.08.1 train for 2026-08-25 with the extended canary plan.
- No feature hold; batching kernel included but gated behind canary and extended telemetry.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Marcus Liu: Triage RLS-1250, open hotfix candidate branch if needed (due 2026-08-19).
- Priya Desai: Draft release notes for v2026.08.1 and collect performance numbers from bench (due 2026-08-22 EOD).
- Elena García: Run mixed-sequence load test (3h) and create/verify canary dashboard (due 2026-08-20).
- Samir Patel: Finish infra autoscaler test, ensure rollback hooks in PR #612, and update runbook (due 2026-08-21).
- Jordan Kim: Finalize canary cohort list and schedule on-call rotation for post-release monitoring (due 2026-08-23).
- K. Novak (SRE): Monitor tokenizer error bucket for hotfix RLS-1245 until 2026-08-20 (ongoing).

Risks / concerns:
- If the batching kernel introduces subtle tail-latency regressions, revert timeline might be tight because several customers rely on improved throughput. We will prefer partial model pinning + rollback only on affected models as first-line mitigation where possible.
- Dedicated customer autoscaler behavior under new kernel is untested at scale - infra tests are high priority.

Follow-ups / next meeting:
- Next release sync: 2026-08-23 10:00 PT (short check-in for canary readiness).
- Full retro planned after 2 weeks of post-release monitoring (tentative 2026-09-08) to capture metrics and customer feedback.

Attachments / references (internal):
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/578
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/612
- JIRA: RLS-1245, RLS-1250
- Canary dashboard (placeholder): grafana.redwood.internal/d/release/canary-v2026.08.1

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep an eye on model-specific P95 - batch changes tend to hide in aggregated metrics.
- Consider enabling sampling traces during canary to get full stack latency breakdowns (Jordan + Elena).

End of notes.
